p.src: The answer cannot be rushed, because the assumption of psychological security is already built into the questioner. We think we have it, or can obtain it, or would collapse without it. It is something to count on, cling to, hold to, or treat as imperishable.

p.src: Because the self that seeks security appears to itself as real. If the self is taken as an actual center, then it must protect itself. The statement that there is no security threatens that center. Thought therefore turns the fact into an idea. As an idea it can be considered, accepted, repeated, resisted, or refined without ending the underlying movement.

p.src: Why does the brain seem to go wild when it is not occupied, and why does mechanical order fail to be real order?

u.src: Why does the brain seem to go wild when it is not occupied, and why does mechanical order fail to be real order?
en: Why does the brain seem to go wild when it is not occupied, and why does mechanical order fail to be real order?

p.src: Answer.

u.src: Answer.

p.src: In occupation there is a kind of order because the brain has content, direction, and repetition. But that order is only mechanical. It depends on the continuity of the process. When the occupation stops, instability returns. If the process continues too long, boredom or dullness appears. If the process is threatened, fear appears. So the order is not free from disorder; it is a way of holding disorder in place.

p.src: Why The Brain Remains Mechanical

p.src: The later dialogue asks a sharper question: why does the brain become mechanical, and why does it remain mechanical? The first answers are partial. Mechanical living is repetitious. It is action and reaction. It is easy. It gives a boundary. It seems safe. But Krishnamurti presses further.

p.src: The brain wants order. Without order it cannot function properly. Since mechanical order is safe for the time being, the brain accepts it and hopes it will not end in disaster. That phrase, for the time being, is important. The mechanical process does give a temporary order; otherwise the brain would not accept it. But temporary order is not total order.

Even revolt can remain mechanical: one leaves a profession, belief, or routine and enters another structure that works in the same way.

p.src: The central late proposition can be stated as follows.

u.src: The central late proposition can be stated as follows.
en: The central late proposition can be stated as follows.

p.src: The mechanical way of living leads to disorder, even though it is adopted in the hope of order.

u.src: The mechanical way of living leads to disorder, even though it is adopted in the hope of order.
en: The mechanical way of living leads to disorder, even though it is adopted in the hope of order.

p.src: Proof. This is not a formal proof in the mathematical sense; it is the ordered argument of the dialogue.

u.src: Proof. This is not a formal proof in the mathematical sense; it is the ordered argument of the dialogue.
en: Proof. This is not a formal proof in the mathematical sense; it is the ordered argument of the dialogue.

p.src: The brain needs order in order to function.

u.src: The brain needs order in order to function.
en: The brain needs order in order to function.

p.src: It accepts a mechanical process because that process gives order for the time being.

u.src: It accepts a mechanical process because that process gives order for the time being.
en: It accepts a mechanical process because that process gives order for the time being.

p.src: The process depends on repetition, continuity, and conditions remaining in place.

u.src: The process depends on repetition, continuity, and conditions remaining in place.
en: The process depends on repetition, continuity, and conditions remaining in place.

p.src: Life disturbs those conditions.

u.src: Life disturbs those conditions.
en: Life disturbs those conditions.

p.src: When the mechanism is disturbed, fear appears.

u.src: When the mechanism is disturbed, fear appears.
en: When the mechanism is disturbed, fear appears.

p.src: To escape that fear, the brain establishes another mechanical habit.

u.src: To escape that fear, the brain establishes another mechanical habit.
en: To escape that fear, the brain establishes another mechanical habit.

p.src: Therefore the original order was not total order; it was disorder maintained under the appearance of order.

u.src: Therefore the original order was not total order; it was disorder maintained under the appearance of order.
en: Therefore the original order was not total order; it was disorder maintained under the appearance of order.

p.src: This is where the dialogue becomes especially delicate. Krishnamurti says that if the whole movement is seen, there is instant action and an order that is not fragmented. A participant immediately objects that this does not yet follow logically. The objection must remain in the chapter. The lecture does not present indestructible order as a completed theorem. It says the matter can be gone into only if the mechanical security developed, attached to, and cultivated by the brain is actually perceived.

p.src: When The Past Meets The Present

u.src: When The Past Meets The Present
en: When The Past Meets The Present

p.src: The final movement brings the whole inquiry into time and relationship. We meet another person through memories, images, reputation, words, pictures, and symbols. With that past, we meet the person now. This is the phrase the dialogue settles on: the past meets the present.

u.src: The final movement brings the whole inquiry into time and relationship. We meet another person through memories, images, reputation, words, pictures, and symbols. With that past, we meet the person now. This is the phrase the dialogue settles on: the past meets the present.

p.src: If the past continues through the present, relationship is mediated by image. The other person may have changed, but the old memory meets him. In that case one does not meet the person; one meets the past. Krishnamurti says that when this movement continues, it is one of the factors of time movement, bondage, fear, and disorder.

p.src: The alternative is not a technique for suppressing memory. The dialogue is more exact than that. It asks whether the movement of the past meeting the present can be completely observed. If it is fully observed, Krishnamurti says, the movement stops. Then there is the possibility of meeting the other as though for the first time.

p.src: The ending is intentionally unfinished. The speakers say they have not really tackled the root: the disturbance, turmoil, travail, anxiety, and wild disorder of the brain. The final question is not decorative. It is the question left for the next inquiry: why do human beings live this way? The final answer named in the dialogue is brief and double: time.

p.src: Summary

u.src: Summary
en: Summary

p.src: The lecture begins with an unfinished question about psychological security and ends with the root problem of time. Its progression is precise. Security is first examined as belief, knowledge, status, property, relationship, and tradition. It is then seen as becoming: the hope that the future will make the self safe. The discussion then turns from idea to fact, from fact to perception, from perception to image, from image to occupation, from occupation to mechanical order, and from mechanical order to the past meeting the present.
